findings.claim: Weighted absolute moment controlled without source tail information

The fixed psi=sqrt(1+x^2) meets Lemma2.13(PDF10): nonnegative C2, subadditive, coercive and bounded first/second derivatives. independent_acceptance.decisive_independent_check: The PDE solution is rho_R(t,x)=integral_0^t partial_x G_(1+s)(x-R)ds. At t=1 its translated profile has sign opposite to x-R; integrating Gaussian derivatives gives absolute mass M=2(sqrt(2)-1)/sqrt(pi) and absolute first moment1. Thus integral psi|rho_R|>=R M-1, while all displayed RHS quantities remain uniformly bounded. Adding fixed G1 to the initial data only subtracts a fixed finite weighted term from this lower bound.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_boundaries: Testing a signed equation against psi controls a signed moment, not this absolute moment. independent_acceptance.repair_check: A Duhamel tail bound exploiting fixed m,c and bounded Dz is a plausible required replacement; it is not supplied or certified in full here. The retained quadrature output agrees with the analytic mass identities and is not an interval enclosure.

For phi_epsilon=epsilon q(x/epsilon), q(0)=0,q'(0)=1, bounded convergence gives mu1({0})=1 and hence ||mu1||TV>=1. The minimal sum is2, achieved by(delta0,delta0). Equality of individual lift norms also gives no control on the norm of their differences.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_boundaries: The closure assertion survives: restriction of representable functionals to(C0^n)* is injective by cutoffs, onto by Hahn-Banach/Riesz on the finite jet product, and isometric using chi(x/R) with derivative errors tending to0. findings.claim: Initial-time weight, mild-sign and arbitrary smoothing exponent corrections
findings.evidence: For t0>0, tau=t-t0, k=1 and gamma=3/2, rho0=partial_xx delta0 gives rho(t)=partial_xx G_tau. The test phi_tau(x)=tau^(1/4) cos(x/sqrt(tau)) has uniformly bounded C_b^(1/2) norm and pairing -exp(-1) tau^(-3/4). The printed t^(3/4) weight therefore diverges at t0; use tau^(3/4). For partial_t u-Lu+H=f, H(u)=u, f=0 and u(0)=1, the printed mild sign gives exp(t) instead of exp(-t). With a nontrivial even standard mollifier, rho=delta0 and test cos(x), the error is (epsilon^2/2) integral y^2 eta(y)dy+o(epsilon^2), contradicting an arbitrary epsilon^delta estimate at delta=3. Gaussian tests use the necessary per-order interpretation of(K), as in P3.
findings.impact: Printed formulas false; time-shift integrability, norm contraction, weaker-dual convergence retained.
